benchmarks.name: EmbodiedBench EB-Navigation
benchmarks.license_status: Ungated. Episodes are 5 JSON files in the GitHub repo. iTHOR scenes come inside the ai2thor 5.0.0 build (Apache-2.0). The EmbodiedBench repo has no LICENSE file: the GitHub API returns license=None, and issue #47 'License clarification' (Sep 2026) is still unanswered.
benchmarks.download: Clone the repo with git-lfs. The ai2thor 5.0.0 Unity build downloads automatically on the first Controller() call. ~/.ai2thor/releases is empty right now, and the build size is unverified.
benchmarks.simulator: AI2-THOR 5.0.0, iTHOR single-room scenes FloorPlan11-330, gridSize 0.1, depth and instance segmentation rendered. 8 actions: move ±0.25 m in 4 directions, rotate 90° (2), tilt 30° (2). Only an action-validity signal comes back as feedback.
benchmarks.python: Env embench_nav: Python 3.9.21, ai2thor 5.0.0, torch 2.5.1, lmdeploy 0.7.0.post2. Already on this machine: ~/miniforge3/envs/embnav_thor (Python 3.9.23, ai2thor 5.0.0).
benchmarks.rendering: CloudRendering (headless Vulkan) is hardcoded in EBNavEnv.py. The README says to fall back to Linux64 (X) if runs time out. The NVIDIA Vulkan ICD and driver 580.126.09 are present, but I did not test-launch it on the RTX 5060.
benchmarks.gpu_mem: Not documented. My unverified estimate is a few hundred MB for THOR at 500x500. The VLM is served separately; issue #29 shows a user running EB evals against a vLLM server.
benchmarks.episodes: 300 = 5 subsets x 60. Base, Common-sense, Complex and Visual reuse the same 60 (scene, target, start pose) tuples with reworded instructions. Long-horizon uses 60 different starts with the target out of view. Max 20 steps. Wall-clock is not published; my estimate is 5-10 h per full run with a local 4-8B VLM.
benchmarks.metrics: Success means final planar distance to the target centre is ≤1.0 m (SUCCESS_THRESHOLD=1, no visibility check). Reported as per-subset and average SR.
benchmarks.best_scores: Paper: GPT-4o 57.7 avg (Long 55.0), InternVL3-78B 53.7. Later: SeeNav-Agent with GPT-4.1 + visual prompt 86.7 (arXiv 2512.02631). EMHO harness search on Qwen3.8-27B-FP8: 75.3 held-out. From the EMHO table: Claude-4.6-Sonnet 62.2, GPT-5 56.8.
benchmarks.small_model_scores: Paper avg (Long): Qwen2-VL-7B 14.0 (3.3), Qwen2.5-VL-7B 20.3 (0.0, via the DashScope API), InternVL2.5-8B 21.3 (0.0), InternVL3-8B 29.3 (5.0). Qwen2.5-VL-7B self-hosted on vLLM: base 35-40, long 5-17 (issue #29). Qwen3.5-9B: 48.7 to 56.7 held-out with EMHO. Qwen2.5-VL-3B + SRGPO RL: 72.3.
ccfa_papers_using_it: EmbodiedBench: Comprehensive Benchmarking MLLMs for Vision-Driven Embodied Agents — ICML 2025 (oral)
VAGEN: Reinforcing World Model Reasoning for Multi-Turn VLM Agents — NeurIPS 2025 (its Navigation env cites EmbodiedBench/AI2-THOR. Base/Common avg: Qwen2.5-VL-3B 0.24, 7B 0.34, VAGEN-Full 0.81)
Not CCF-A main track: EMHO is a NeurIPS 2026 workshop paper. SeeNav-Agent and BrainMem are arXiv only.
failure_modes: Small models collapse when the target starts out of view: Long-subset SR is 0.0 for Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL2.5-8B, 5.0 for InternVL3-8B.
The paper's error analysis finds missed or hallucinated targets that lead to early stops, flawed path logic, weak reflection, and miscounted steps.
EMHO traces show repeated blocked moves and ineffective loops; 10% of runs had 5 or more consecutive rotations.
Chat history behaves inconsistently: it lifts InternVL2.5-8B from 5.7 to 21.3, while Qwen2-VL-7B does better without it (16.3 vs 14.0). Detection boxes and multi-view input hurt navigation.

benchmarks.name: EmbodiedBench EB-Habitat
benchmarks.license_status: Ungated. Assets come from habitat_sim datasets_download 'rearrange_task_assets': ReplicaCAD (CC-BY-4.0), YCB (CC-BY-4.0), hab_fetch (CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0), plus two zips from dl.fbaipublicfiles.com (HTTP 200). It needs neither HSSD nor HM3D. Episode pickles are in the repo, and the code is derived from apple/ml-llarp.
benchmarks.download: About 0.9 GB: ReplicaCAD 0.16 GB, YCB 0.50 GB, hab_fetch 0.03 GB, rearrange_pick v0 0.012 GB, replica_cad rearrange v1 0.21 GB. Sizes are from the HF API and HTTP HEAD.
benchmarks.simulator: Habitat 2.0: habitat-sim 0.3.0 (withbullet, headless) with habitat-lab v0.3.0. Fetch robot in a language-rearrangement (LLaRP) config. 70 high-level skills (navigate, pick, place, open, close).
benchmarks.python: Env embench: Python 3.9.20, torch 2.4.0, lmdeploy 0.6.3. The local ~/miniforge3/envs/embnav has habitat-sim 0.3.3, not the pinned 0.3.0, and I haven't checked API compatibility.
benchmarks.rendering: Headless EGL build of habitat-sim. No X server needed.
benchmarks.gpu_mem: Not documented. Rendering ReplicaCAD should be light (unverified estimate).
benchmarks.episodes: 300 = 6 subsets x 50 (Base, Common-sense, Complex, Spatial, Visual, Long-horizon). Max 30 steps. An episode ends after more than 10 invalid actions. long_horizon.pickle was updated in place, with the old version kept as long_horizon_old.pickle.
benchmarks.metrics: Task success rate, average and per subset.
benchmarks.best_scores: Paper: Claude-3.5-Sonnet 68.0, GPT-4o 59.0, Claude-3.7 58.7, InternVL3-78B 55.0. ORBIT re-run: Claude-3.5 70.4. Mimir (arXiv 2608.04933) claims 86.0 on the Long subset with an unverified backbone.
benchmarks.small_model_scores: Paper: Qwen2-VL-7B 18.3, Qwen2.5-VL-7B 14.3 (API), InternVL2.5-8B 11.3, InternVL3-8B 24.3. RoboGPT-R1's reproduction: Qwen2.5-VL-3B 14.67, 7B 15.0. Qwen2.5-VL-7B self-hosted scores 42-50 on Base (#29). Models trained on ALFRED, tested out of domain: ORBIT-7B 22.4, RoboGPT-R1-3B 22.0, VAGEN-3B 11.2, WAP-7B 9.6.
ccfa_papers_using_it: EmbodiedBench — ICML 2025
ORBIT: On-Policy Reinforcement Fine-Tuning with Offline Reward for Multi-Step Embodied Planning — ACL 2026 (uses EB-Habitat as the unseen, out-of-domain environment)
Not CCF-A: RoboGPT-R1 ('Enhancing Robot Task Planning with RL') — AAMAS 2026, which is CCF-B per notes_scratch.txt
failure_modes: Small models are near zero on Common-sense and Long (Qwen2.5-VL-7B 2/2, InternVL2.5-8B 4/2).
JSON format errors average 4.40 per trajectory for InternVL2.5-8B. Self-hosted Qwen2.5-VL-7B has an invalid-action ratio of 0.29-0.38.
Planners trained on ALFRED transfer poorly here (9.6-22.4).
Issue #37: initial states are non-deterministic even with a fixed seed. Issue #39: long-horizon scenes didn't match their instructions (now closed).

benchmarks.name: EmbodiedBench EB-ALFRED
benchmarks.license_status: Ungated. HF dataset EmbodiedBench/EB-ALFRED (gated=False, license tag apache-2.0). Scenes come with the ai2thor 2.1.0 build (Apache-2.0). The EmbodiedBench code repo itself has no LICENSE file (issue #47).
benchmarks.download: 0.54 GB from HF, 1,269 files of ALFRED json_2.1.0 trajectories, plus the ai2thor 2.1.0 build, which downloads automatically (size unverified).
benchmarks.simulator: AI2-THOR 2.1.0 through a ThorConnector based on LoTa-Bench. 8 skill types expanded into 171-298 dynamic actions (find, pick up, put down, open, close, turn on/off, slice).
benchmarks.python: Env embench: Python 3.9.20, ai2thor 2.1.0, torch 2.4.0. The pinned torch doesn't support sm_120, so the VLM should be served from a separate CUDA 12.8 env through an OpenAI-compatible API.
benchmarks.rendering: Needs an X server. X_DISPLAY='1' is hardcoded in EBAlfEnv.py, and the repo ships a startx.py script for it. This desktop already has DISPLAY=:1, so it should work there without sudo (not tested). No CloudRendering.
benchmarks.gpu_mem: Not documented. My estimate for Unity on X is a few hundred MB (unverified).
benchmarks.episodes: 300 = 6 subsets x 50 (Base, Common-sense, Complex, Visual, Spatial, Long-horizon). Max 30 steps. Episodes stop after more than 10 invalid actions or an empty plan. A later fix stops 'find' from teleporting the agent; commit 5fdee37 reproduces the paper's numbers.
benchmarks.metrics: Task success rate per subset and averaged. Some papers also report subgoal success rate.
benchmarks.best_scores: Paper: Claude-3.7-Sonnet 67.7, Claude-3.5 64.0, Gemini-1.5-Pro 62.3, GPT-4o 56.3. Trained 3-7B models: ORBIT-7B 72.4 (5 subsets, no Long), ERA-3B 65.2 (5 subsets), WAP-7B 62.7, RoboGPT-R1-3B 55.33.
benchmarks.small_model_scores: Zero-shot, from the paper: Qwen2-VL-7B 1.7, Qwen2.5-VL-7B 4.7, InternVL2.5-8B 2.0, InternVL3-8B 10.3, Llama-3.2-11B-V 13.7, Gemma-3-12B 25.7. Qwen2.5-VL-3B scores 0 (ERA) or 1.33 (RoboGPT-R1). Self-hosted Qwen2.5-VL-7B scores 0-6 per subset (#29), lower than the API numbers.
ccfa_papers_using_it: EmbodiedBench — ICML 2025
World-aware Planning Narratives Enhance Large Vision-Language Model Planner (WAP) — NeurIPS 2025
ORBIT — ACL 2026 (Tongji; ties to the REBP repo)
ERA: Transforming VLMs into Embodied Agents via Embodied Prior Learning and Online RL — has an OpenReview forum, acceptance unverified
failure_modes: Zero-shot 7-8B models almost never succeed. InternVL2.5-8B makes 8.04 JSON format errors per trajectory.
Models keep generating empty plans until the episode is cut off. Self-hosted Qwen2.5-VL-7B has an invalid-action ratio of 0.52-0.80 (#29).
Issue #43: 'find' can report success even when the target isn't visible.
Trained SOTA overfits: ALFRED-trained models drop to 9.6-22.4 on EB-Habitat.

benchmarks.name: EmbodiedBench EB-Manipulation
benchmarks.license_status: Ungated. The HF dataset EmbodiedBench/EB-Manipulation has gated=False and no license tag. The install script fetches CoppeliaSim_Pro_V4_1_0. Whether the Pro build is licensed for this use is unverified. The CoppeliaSim 4.1 Edu build is free for education.
benchmarks.download: 2.0 GB for the HF dataset (690 files), plus the CoppeliaSim 4.1 tarball (size unverified), PyRep, and RLBench/VLMBench-style task files.
benchmarks.simulator: CoppeliaSim 4.1.0 with PyRep and a Franka Panda arm. Actions are 7-D: xyz in 100 bins, roll/pitch/yaw in 120 bins, plus a gripper bit.
benchmarks.python: Env embench_man: Python 3.9.19, torch 2.4.0, lmdeploy 0.6.4. Requires COPPELIASIM_ROOT, LD_LIBRARY_PATH and QT_QPA_PLATFORM_PLUGIN_PATH.
benchmarks.rendering: Needs a display (the verify step uses export DISPLAY=:1). Headless use would require Xvfb or the desktop X server.
benchmarks.episodes: 228 tasks: Base, Common, Complex and Spatial have 48 each, Visual has 36. There is no Long subset. Max 15 steps.
benchmarks.metrics: Task success rate per subset and averaged.
benchmarks.best_scores: Paper: GPT-4o 28.9, Claude-3.7 28.5. Later: ERA-3B 48.3, EMHO on Qwen3.8-27B 39.4 held-out (44.2 on the search split), Claude-4.6-Sonnet 37.6 (from the EMHO table).
benchmarks.small_model_scores: Qwen2-VL-7B 0.0 on every subset, Qwen2.5-VL-7B 9.6, InternVL2.5-8B 7.0, InternVL3-8B 11.5, Llama-3.2-11B 0.9, Gemma-3-12B 20.6. Qwen3.5-9B goes from 10.7 to 21.0 with EMHO. Robot-R1 (7B) scores 11.7 (cited by ERA).
ccfa_papers_using_it: EmbodiedBench — ICML 2025
ERA reports EB-Manipulation, but its venue is unverified. EMHO is a NeurIPS 2026 workshop paper.
failure_modes: Producing precise discretized 7-D poses is the main bottleneck.
Multi-step and multi-view images hurt performance. Detection boxes add about 10.
EMHO traces show the agent restarting the full grasp sequence instead of resuming, grasping at the same coordinates again (30%), and ignoring reward feedback.
Install friction: issue #20 reports failures installing embench_man, and reinstalling PyRep overwrites the Lua add-on.

benchmarks.name: RoboTHOR ObjectNav (2021 challenge splits)
benchmarks.license_status: Ungated. The robothor-challenge repo and AI2-THOR are both Apache-2.0. Episodes are bundled in the repo. The leaderboard is at leaderboard.allenai.org/robothor_objectnav.
benchmarks.download: Clone the repo. Get the THOR build with robothor_challenge/scripts/download_thor_build.py (size unverified).
benchmarks.simulator: AI2-THOR 2.7.2 for the AllenAct path. 15 val apartments (train/val/test-challenge). Actions are MoveAhead 0.25 m, Rotate 30°, LookUp/Down, and Stop.
benchmarks.python: Not stated in the README. AllenAct requires Python 3.6+. Newer pipelines such as procthor-rl run it on Python 3.9 with a pinned ai2thor commit.
benchmarks.rendering: The README says a GPU is required and gives an X11/Docker route. Newer ai2thor builds can render it with CloudRendering, as procthor-rl does with evaluation.tasks=robothor.
benchmarks.episodes: Val 1,800 (15 scenes, 12 categories). Test 2,040 with no shortest paths. Train 108k. Max 500 steps. CogNav's timing works out to about 9 min per episode with API LLM/VLM calls (my estimate). A full val run with a VLM called every step would take days.
benchmarks.metrics: SR, SPL, proximity-only SR/SPL, and episode length. Success = Stop issued within 1 m with the target visible.
benchmarks.best_scores: Zero-shot: STRIVE 68.1 SR / 36.3 SPL (gemini-2.0-flash, arXiv). CogNav 54.6 / 24.3 (GPT-3/4v, ICCV 2025). SG-Nav-GPT 47.5 / 24.0. Trained: ProcTHOR fine-tuned 65.2 / 28.8.
benchmarks.small_model_scores: SG-Nav-LLaMA-7B with LLaVA-1.6-Mistral-7B: 47.3 SR / 23.7 SPL. CoW with OWL-ViT B/16 (no LLM): 27.5 / 17.2. VLTNet (GPT-3.5): 33.2 SR. I found no sub-9B Qwen-VL or InternVL agent numbers.
ccfa_papers_using_it: CogNav: Cognitive Process Modeling for Object Goal Navigation with LLMs — ICCV 2025 (HM3D + MP3D + RoboTHOR)
Online 3D Scene Graph Prompting for LLM-based Zero-shot Object Navigation (SG-Nav) — NeurIPS 2024
CoWs on Pasture — CVPR 2023
In recent CCF-A papers RoboTHOR shows up only as a secondary set next to HM3D/MP3D, never on its own.
failure_modes: The stop decision is critical: success needs the target visible and within 1 m.
CogNav on HM3D attributes 35.7% of failures to persistent detection failures and 64.3% to unreachable targets, so detection is the part a method can fix.
Per-step LLM agents are slow: CogNav needs about 230 scene-graph updates per episode.
Small targets such as AlarmClock, SprayBottle and Mug are probably hard to detect (my inference, unverified).

benchmarks.name: ProcTHOR-10k / ArchitecTHOR ObjectNav
benchmarks.license_status: Ungated. procthor, prior and procthor-rl are Apache-2.0. allenai/procthor-10k is a public git repo (I confirmed with git ls-remote). prior.load_dataset fetches it through git-lfs. An optional GitHub token avoids rate limits.
benchmarks.download: procthor-10k comes over git-lfs (size unverified). ArchitecTHOR's 10 houses are distributed through the ai2thor/procthor-rl evaluation tasks; I didn't confirm exactly how.
benchmarks.simulator: AI2-THOR with a commit pinned in procthor-rl (0+ca10d107...). ProcTHOR-10k has 10,000/1,000/1,000 train/val/test houses. ArchitecTHOR has 10 artist-designed houses and is test-only.
benchmarks.python: procthor-rl: Python 3.9, torch 2.0.1, open_clip_torch, objaverse, objathor.
benchmarks.gpu_mem: Not documented. The training examples use 96 processes, which implies a multi-GPU node; evaluation alone is light.
benchmarks.episodes: I didn't extract episode counts for ProcTHOR val or ArchitecTHOR (unverified).
benchmarks.best_scores: From the ProcTHOR paper: ArchitecTHOR 0-shot 31.4 SR / 0.195 SPL, iTHOR 0-shot 75.7, fine-tuned 77.5. Supervised trained policies only.
benchmarks.small_model_scores: I found no zero-shot LLM/VLM-agent numbers on ProcTHOR-10k val or ArchitecTHOR in 2024-2026 work.
ccfa_papers_using_it: ProcTHOR: Large-Scale Embodied AI Using Procedural Generation — NeurIPS 2022 (from memory, not re-verified)
I found no 2025-2026 CCF-A paper that uses ArchitecTHOR or ProcTHOR-10k val as its ObjectNav benchmark.
failure_modes: Large cross-dataset gap: ProcTHOR 0-shot gets 55.0 on RoboTHOR but only 9.0 on HM3D.
With only 10 training houses the policy reaches 11.3 SR on ArchitecTHOR, against 27.0 with 10k houses.

benchmarks.name: CHORES-S ObjectNav (SPOC, ProcTHOR-Objaverse houses)
benchmarks.license_status: Ungated. spoc-robot-training is Apache-2.0. objathor assets and houses download through plain python -m scripts, with no token or registration in the README. Objaverse terms are per asset (unverified here).
benchmarks.download: Objathor assets version 2023_07_28 (about 39.7k asset dirs) plus val houses (val.jsonl.gz). Sizes are not stated.
benchmarks.simulator: AI2-THOR commit 0+5d0ab8ab... with Objaverse assets in ProcTHOR houses. Stretch-style agent.
benchmarks.python: Python 3.9 or later. The ai2thor commit build installs from ai2thor-pypi.allenai.org.
benchmarks.rendering: Not stated in the README. CloudRendering is probable (unverified).
benchmarks.episodes: The official ObjectNav split has 200 trajectories in 200 test houses (per RoboTron-Nav).
benchmarks.best_scores: RoboTron-Nav 81.1 SR / 43.9 SEL (ICCV 2025). RING 72.1. SPOC* 60.0. EmbSigLIP 36.5. PIRLNav 20.0. PoliFormer reports 85.5 SR on CHORES-S (arXiv 2406.20083), which conflicts with RoboTron-Nav's SOTA claim; the setting likely differs.
benchmarks.small_model_scores: Only trained policies are reported. I found no training-free sub-9B VLM agent numbers.
ccfa_papers_using_it: RoboTron-Nav: A Unified Framework for Embodied Navigation Integrating Perception, Planning, and Prediction — ICCV 2025
Not CCF-A: The One RING (ICRA 2026, per the author's site), PoliFormer (CoRL)
failure_modes: SPOC keeps re-searching the same paths when the target is in another room (RoboTron-Nav Fig. 5).

benchmarks.name: Pasture (CoWs on Pasture, L-ZSON)
benchmarks.license_status: Ungated. Direct downloads from cow.cs.columbia.edu return HTTP 200 with no registration. The real-stanford/cow repo has no LICENSE file. Only the optional Habitat MP3D part needs a Matterport request.
benchmarks.download: pasture_builds.tar.gz 2.13 GB plus datasets.tar.gz 0.18 GB (sizes from HTTP HEAD).
benchmarks.simulator: Custom AI2-THOR builds of the 15 RoboTHOR val rooms with uncommon objects, extra instances as distractors, and hidden targets. Uses AllenAct.
benchmarks.python: conda environment.yml (env 'cow'). Tested with CUDA 11.2. Python version not stated.
benchmarks.rendering: Xorg on each GPU (sudo python scripts/startx.py). The desktop X on :1 might work instead (unverified).
benchmarks.gpu_mem: Not documented. The authors used 8x RTX 2080.
benchmarks.episodes: 2,520 = 7 splits x 360 (12 objects x 15 rooms x 2 starts): uncommon, appearance, spatial, appearance+distractor, spatial+distractor, hidden, hidden+distractor.
benchmarks.metrics: SR, SPL (VLTNet uses SWPL). Success = Stop within 1 m with the target visible.
benchmarks.best_scores: VLTNet (GPT-3.5 + GLIP, arXiv only): 28.2 avg SR. CoW with OWL B/32: 21.1 SR / 12.6 SPL.
benchmarks.small_model_scores: No ≤9B LLM/VLM agent numbers. All CoW variants use CLIP/OWL only, with no LLM.
ccfa_papers_using_it: CoWs on Pasture: Baselines and Benchmarks for Language-Driven Zero-Shot Object Navigation — CVPR 2023
I found no 2025-2026 CCF-A paper that evaluates on Pasture.
failure_modes: CoWs struggle to use attribute and spatial language and do relatively well on uncommon objects.
Distractor and hidden splits are the hardest (16-19 SR).

benchmarks.name: ALFWorld (text, TextWorld)
benchmarks.license_status: Ungated. MIT license. The bundled Fast Downward planner is GPL-3.0. alfworld-download needs no registration.
benchmarks.download: alfworld-download fetches the PDDL and game files plus a MaskRCNN detector into ~/.cache/alfworld. Size is not stated.
benchmarks.simulator: TextWorld (AlfredTWEnv). CPU only. Admissible commands available.
benchmarks.python: Python 3.9 or later. pip install alfworld (text only) or alfworld[full].
benchmarks.gpu_mem: Only for the LLM. A 4-bit 7-8B model fits in 8 GB.
benchmarks.episodes: valid_seen 140 and valid_unseen 134 (3,553 train games), six task types. GiGPO caps episodes at 50 steps.
benchmarks.metrics: Success rate overall and per task type (Pick, Look, Clean, Heat, Cool, Pick2).
benchmarks.best_scores: Trained: GiGPO Qwen2.5-7B 90.8, 1.5B 86.7. Prompting: Gemini-2.5-Pro 60.3, GPT-4o 48.0 (GiGPO table). Training-free self-evolution with EvoEmbody (Qwen 27B/4B pair) reaches 93.3 held-out (NeurIPS 2026 workshop).
benchmarks.small_model_scores: Qwen2.5-1.5B: base 4.1, ReAct 12.8, Reflexion 21.8, GRPO 72.8. Qwen2.5-7B: base 14.8, ReAct 31.2, Reflexion 42.7, PPO 80.4, GRPO 77.6 (GiGPO Table 1, 3 seeds).
ccfa_papers_using_it: Group-in-Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training (GiGPO) — NeurIPS 2025
Commonly used in LLM-agent RL and memory papers. It is text only, not visual navigation.
failure_modes: Base small models are weakest on Cool, Heat and Pick2 (Qwen2.5-7B: 2.8, 6.9 and 3.2).
EvoEmbody names the bottlenecks as inventory tracking, state-conditioned matching and spatial coordination.
The benchmark is close to saturated (87-93%), which leaves little room for a robust gain.

benchmarks.name: ALFWorld (visual, AI2-THOR / RL4VLM setting)
benchmarks.download: Same as the text version plus the THOR build. Size unverified.
benchmarks.simulator: AlfredThorEnv on AI2-THOR. RL4VLM feeds an RGB image plus a prompt with the admissible actions.
benchmarks.rendering: Needs an OpenGL X server. The README uses startx.py with sudo, or DISPLAY can point at an existing X server.
benchmarks.episodes: Same 140/134 eval splits. I didn't extract the episode count RL4VLM uses (unverified).
benchmarks.metrics: Success rate per task type, weighted by task frequency.
benchmarks.best_scores: RL4VLM (LLaVA-1.6-Mistral-7B with PPO) 21.7, GPT-4V 19.4, Gemini 13.5. BUTLER with expert data 37.0 (these rows look inconsistent in the extraction). GTR (ICCV 2025) claims 3-5x higher success than much larger SOTA models.
benchmarks.small_model_scores: LLaVA-1.6-7B: SFT 17.7, RL4VLM 21.7, RL without CoT 16.3.
ccfa_papers_using_it: Fine-Tuning Large Vision-Language Models as Decision-Making Agents via RL (RL4VLM) — NeurIPS 2024
GTR: Guided Thought Reinforcement Prevents Thought Collapse in RL-based VLM Agent Training — ICCV 2025
failure_modes: Outcome-only RL causes thought collapse: reasoning diversity drops and invalid actions rise.
SFT-only LLaVA scores 0 on Look and Cool.

benchmarks.name: Embodied-Reasoner interactive search benchmark (AI2-THOR)
benchmarks.license_status: Ungated. The HF dataset zwq2018/embodied_reasoner has gated=False and no license tag. The repo is Mulan PSL v2. Where the 809-task test set lives (repo or HF) is unverified.
benchmarks.download: The HF dataset is 157 GB (38 files, mostly training images). The evaluation framework is in embodied_reasoner/evaluate/.
benchmarks.simulator: AI2-THOR, version not stated. 12 held-out scenes. High-level actions: navigate to, pickup, put in, toggle, open, close, observe, move forward, end.
benchmarks.python: Not stated. Each subproject has its own environment.
benchmarks.episodes: 809 test tasks across Search, Manipulate, Transport and Composite (11 subtypes), including 25 ultra-long tasks of 14-27 key actions.
benchmarks.metrics: Success rate, search efficiency (key actions over predicted actions), task completeness.
ccfa_papers_using_it: Embodied-Reasoner: Synergizing Visual Search, Reasoning, and Action for Embodied Interactive Tasks — ACL 2026 (benchmark paper; no other users found)
failure_modes: Repeated searching: re-checking containers inspected a few steps earlier. On Composite tasks, repetitive exploration is 54% for o3-mini and 43% for Qwen2-VL-72B.
Forgetting the task and logical inconsistency.
SFT 7B models give up too early with 'object does not exist'.

benchmarks.name: EmbodiedEval
benchmarks.license_status: Ungated. The HF dataset EmbodiedEval/EmbodiedEval has gated=False and a cc0-1.0 tag. The repo is MIT. Scenes include HSSD-derived houses, redistributed inside the dataset; I did not check that the redistribution complies with HSSD terms.
benchmarks.download: 19.6 GB (HF API). The README says about 20 GB.
benchmarks.simulator: LEGENT (Unity). 328 tasks in 125 scenes from Objaverse-synthetic, AI2-THOR, HSSD and Sketchfab. Navigation-graph movement plus open-vocabulary interaction choices.
benchmarks.rendering: Xorg with nvidia-xconfig on servers (sudo). Alternatively, run the simulator on a local display and use --remote.
benchmarks.gpu_mem: Not documented. The config example uses an RTX 3090.
benchmarks.episodes: 328 tasks across Navigation, Object interaction, Social, Attribute QA and Spatial QA. Max 24 steps.
ccfa_papers_using_it: EmbodiedEval: Evaluate Multimodal LLMs as Embodied Agents — CVPR 2026 Workshop, not CCF-A
failure_modes: Hallucinated or missed objects, insufficient exploration and over-confident early answers, weak egocentric spatial reasoning, aimless circling and repeated pickups. Small models are near 0% on object interaction.

benchmarks.name: VLABench
benchmarks.license_status: Repo is MIT. Assets come via scripts/download_assets.py (source unspecified); gating unverified.
benchmarks.simulator: MuJoCo 3.2.2 with dm_control 1.0.22 (requirements.txt). 100 task categories, 2,000+ objects.

ranking: 1. EB-Navigation (primary). This is the clearest VLM-navigation benchmark at an ICML 2025 oral, and VAGEN at NeurIPS 2025 also uses it. It is ungated and renders headless through CloudRendering, and the ai2thor 5.0.0 env is already installed. Small models are weak (14-37) against a frontier of 58-87, and they fail in identifiable ways: target out of view on Long, loops. A full run takes hours. Main risk: only 120 unique start configurations.

2. EB-Habitat (primary, paired with #1). It is ungated (ReplicaCAD, about 0.9 GB) and EGL headless. Planners trained on ALFRED collapse here (9.6-22.4), which supports a training-free generalization story. Self-hosted 7B models score 42-50 on Base but near 0 on Common and Long, so the failure modes are visible.

3. EB-ALFRED (third EB environment, for reviewer comparability). It has the most CCF-A users: EmbodiedBench, WAP at NeurIPS 2025, ORBIT at ACL 2026. It needs X, and :1 is available. Zero-shot small models score 2-10, while trained 3-7B SOTA reaches 55-72, so a training-free method has to be framed against the trained methods.

4. RoboTHOR ObjectNav val (secondary or real-robot-adjacent). It is ungated, and CogNav (ICCV 2025) and SG-Nav (NeurIPS 2024) report on it, including a LLaMA-7B baseline at 47.3 SR. But 1,800 episodes x 500 steps is slow for per-step VLM agents. Reviewers treat it as secondary to HM3D/MP3D, so it should not be the only benchmark.

5. Embodied-Reasoner benchmark (809 AI2-THOR search tasks, ACL 2026). Small-versus-large gap is large (Qwen2-VL-7B 14.8 vs GPT-4o 66.7) and the failure mode is clear (repeated search). But nobody else uses it, the data is 157 GB, and the test-set location is unverified.
6. ALFWorld visual (RL4VLM / GTR setting). It is ungated and accepted at NeurIPS 2024 and ICCV 2025. The ceiling is low (about 20-22), but it is a niche setting and needs X.

7. ALFWorld text. Cheap, CPU only, and standard for agent RL (GiGPO, NeurIPS 2025). But it has no vision or navigation and is close to saturated (87-93), so it is only an optional fourth benchmark for a memory or planning angle.
8. CHORES-S ObjectNav (ICCV 2025 RoboTron-Nav). It is ungated, but every reported result is a trained policy and there is no training-free VLM baseline to compare against.
9. EmbodiedEval. It is ungated (CC0, 19.6 GB) and covers navigation and QA, but the venue is a CVPR 2026 Workshop and only 328 tasks across 5 types are available.
10. Pasture. It is ungated (2.3 GB), but I found no 2025-2026 CCF-A uptake.
11. ProcTHOR-10k / ArchitecTHOR. Ungated, but it has no zero-shot VLM baselines and no recent CCF-A use.
12. EB-Manipulation, VLABench, EAI, ET-Plan-Bench. These are manipulation or symbolic tasks, or have unverified venues. They are off-target for an agent and navigation paper.
notes: RECOMMENDED SUITE: EB-Navigation + EB-Habitat as the main pair, plus EB-ALFRED. All three are ungated, share one harness and prompts, and run locally on a 4-8B VLM. Optionally add a fixed, seeded RoboTHOR val subset with the full split reported for the final method, plus the LTR M1 demo, as the 'real navigation' bridge. A RoboTHOR-only ObjectNav paper risks reviewers asking for HM3D/MP3D.

REPRODUCIBILITY TRAP (issue #29): EmbodiedBench's Qwen2.5-VL numbers came from Alibaba's DashScope API, and some requests were blocked by policy filters. On self-hosted vLLM, Qwen2.5-VL-7B scores higher on Habitat and Navigation (Habitat base 42-50 vs 32, Nav base 35-40 vs 20) and lower on ALFRED. The maintainers say to use your own reproduced numbers. Re-run every baseline locally with the same server and prompts, and report mean±std over several seeds.

STATISTICAL POWER: EB-Nav Base, Common, Complex and Visual share the same 60 (scene, target, start) tuples and differ only in wording. Long adds 60 distinct starts. So there are about 120 independent configurations, and success is lenient (planar distance ≤1 m, no visibility check). EB-ALFRED and EB-Habitat subsets are 50 episodes, so one episode is 2 points. Use bootstrap CIs, paired tests and several seeds. Habitat initial states are non-deterministic (#37).

CROWDED NOVELTY SPACE on EmbodiedBench. Training-free work: BrainMem (all 4 envs), Mimir (ALFRED/Habitat), RoboMemory (72B), EMHO harness optimization (Nav/Man, Qwen 9B/27B), SeeNav visual prompting (86.7 with GPT-4.1). Trained work: ERA, ORBIT, WAP, RoboGPT-R1, VAGEN, SeeNav-SRGPO. A new method has to be clearly different from memory, reflection, harness search and visual prompts, and should be compared against at least one from each category.

LICENSE NUANCE: the EmbodiedBench code repo has no LICENSE file, and issue #47 (Sep 2026) is unanswered. EB-ALFRED data is tagged apache-2.0, and EB-Manipulation has no tag. There is no registration or gate. Running it and publishing scores is standard practice. Cite it and don't redistribute.

DISPLAY=:1 with X0/X1 sockets, NVIDIA Vulkan ICD present, driver 580.126.09, RTX 5060 at 8151 MiB with 1182 MiB used at idle. I did not launch a THOR build, to avoid colliding with those installers.

SOFTWARE PINS: the EB envs pin torch 2.4-2.5 and lmdeploy 0.6-0.7, which have no sm_120 kernels. Keep the simulator envs CPU-side and point EmbodiedBench's remote_url/OpenAI client at a separate CUDA 12.8 vLLM or llama.cpp server. Issue #29 shows a user running all EB evals on vLLM. EB-ALFRED needs ai2thor 2.1.0 and its own env; that is a separate env from embnav_thor.

WALL-CLOCK (my estimate, unverified): EB-Nav runs up to 20 VLM calls per episode, so 300 episodes take about 5-10 h with a 4-bit 4-8B model. ALFRED and Habitat use multi-step plans; ORBIT reports about 4-14 planner steps per task, so about 3-8 h per run. RoboTHOR val at 500 steps per episode is 10-100x more expensive unless the VLM is called sparsely, as in VLFM-style value maps.

VENUE TIERS: notes_scratch.txt (CCF 2026 list) puts IJCAI at CCF-B and AAMAS at B. ICML, ICCV, ACM MM, AAAI, CVPR, NeurIPS, ICLR and ACL are A. CVPR/NeurIPS workshop papers (EmbodiedEval, EMHO, EvoEmbody) are not CCF-A, but reviewers will still expect them cited as prior art.

INCONSISTENCIES SEEN: ORBIT's table lists 'ERA-7B 67.2', but the ERA paper only reports ERA-3B (65.2). RoboTron-Nav claims SOTA at 81.1 on CHORES-S while PoliFormer reports 85.5. The setting probably differs; I didn't verify. WAP's '+60.7' is against a closed-loop baseline of 2, not the paper's 4.7. EmbodiedBench text vs table on Claude manipulation. Two EB-Nav values (17.0, 16.0) aren't multiples of 1/60.
